brief.headline: Memory pricing power intact as HBM supply-demand mismatch persists through 2027; hyperscaler capex run-rate sustains despite equity volatility
brief.summary: <cite index="10-1,17-1,17-2">DRAM contract prices are rising 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, with NAND up 10-15%, marking a deceleration from Q1's record 93-98% spike but extending the rally into its fifth consecutive quarter.</cite> <cite index="2-2,2-3,2-9">HBM3E spot pricing holds near $300/stack, with SK Hynix commanding 50-55% market share and HBM4 expected to launch Q3 2026 at ~$500/stack.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-10">Industry consensus points toward manufacturers sharply raising HBM quotes in 2027, with potential for prices to double as HBM will account for 30% of total DRAM wafer starts, intensifying crowding-out effects.</cite> <cite index="20-3,24-2,24-5">Hyperscaler capex from Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft totals ~$725B in 2026, up 77% YoY, with the overwhelming majority directed to AI data centers and Nvidia GPU purchases.</cite> <cite index="31-10">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from 20% currently to about 10% by end-2026, though lead times for HBM3E stacks remain at 20-26 weeks.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="2-3,2-9">SK Hynix maintains 50-55% HBM market share and clear technology lead on HBM3E qualification with Nvidia.</cite> <cite index="43-8">Samsung holds 35% HBM market share in Q3 2025 compared to SK Hynix's 53%, though Samsung co-CEO noted customers stating 'Samsung is back' on HBM4.</cite> <cite index="46-7">SK Hynix is the leading supplier of advanced HBM chips to Nvidia, while Samsung has been investing heavily to narrow the technology gap.</cite> Tactical edge to SK Hynix on allocation certainty and HBM3E ramp; Samsung catching up on HBM4 but qualification timeline remains binary risk. Both benefit from structural DRAM/NAND undersupply, but SK Hynix trades at a steeper multiple reflecting the Nvidia socket lock. <cite index="41-13,47-1,47-3">Recent volatility saw SK Hynix drop 11.5-14.57% in single sessions tracking U.S. chip selloffs, while Samsung fell 7-9%.</cite> Post-Nasdaq ADR listing on July 10, SK Hynix liquidity improves but ADR premium creates two-way risk.

memory_cycle.stage: mid-cycle undersupply with 2027 peak pricing in sight
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-10,13-12">Q1 2026 DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ, pushing total memory industry revenue up 81% QoQ to $97 billion.</cite> <cite index="8-3,9-16,9-17">Server DDR5 profitability overtook HBM in Q1 2026 for the first time, with DDR5 64GB RDIMM surpassing HBM per-wafer revenue and profit margins.</cite> <cite index="15-22,15-25">Hyperscaler capex among top eight CSPs projected to exceed $600 billion in 2026, a 40% YoY increase, with Micron noting a 3-to-1 conversion ratio between HBM and DDR5 wafer capacity.</cite> <cite index="13-17,13-18">TrendForce expects meaningful new NAND supply not until late 2027 or 2028, while global smartphone shipments are expected to fall 14% in 2026.</cite> Demand destruction visible in consumer segments but AI-driven enterprise demand setting the price. New fab capacity from Samsung P5 (2028), SK Hynix M15X (mid-2027), and M17 NAND (H1 2029) still 12-36 months out.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1,1-2,1-8">HBM now represents 30-40% of total AI accelerator manufacturing cost, up from under 20% two generations ago; for the B200 with eight HBM3e stacks, memory alone costs $2,400, exceeding the logic die cost.</cite> <cite index="1-11">Lead times for HBM3E stacks remain at 20-26 weeks.</cite> <cite index="6-1,6-2">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026, with HBM3E supply remaining tight as manufacturers prioritize ramping HBM4 production.</cite> <cite index="9-4,9-5,9-21">2026 HBM demand is fueled by AI ASIC capacity upgrades (96/192GB to 216/288GB per chip), while 2027 will be driven by Nvidia's Rubin Ultra platform; TrendForce estimates HBM will account for 30% of total DRAM wafer starts in 2027.</cite> <cite index="43-1,43-5">Samsung and SK Hynix struck a deal with OpenAI for the eventual supply of 900,000 DRAM wafers a month for the Stargate project.</cite> Supply tightness structural through 2027 despite TSMC CoWoS capacity expansion; pricing power firmly with suppliers.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR debut creates two-way volatility; stock whipsaws 27% surge to 5% drop in consecutive sessions
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="45-1,45-11,45-12">ADR whipsawed from 27% surge Tuesday to 5% drop, reflecting thin float, ADR premium to Seoul-listed shares, and heavy demand from newly launched leveraged products.</cite> <cite index="41-3">SK Hynix set to begin trading ADRs on Nasdaq July 10.</cite> Near-term trading noise but improves U.S. investor access and index inclusion optionality.

news_pulse.headline: South Korea announces 800 trillion won ($518B) national semiconductor project; Samsung and SK Hynix each to build two new fabs
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="46-1,46-2">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix will each build two new semiconductor fabrication plants in South Korea's southwest as part of an 800 trillion won ($518 billion) national ecosystem project.</cite> <cite index="41-14,41-15">SK Hynix plans to invest 100 trillion won, allocating 80 trillion won to M17 NAND plant (operations H1 2029) and 20 trillion won to P&T7 advanced packaging facility.</cite> Validates long-term capacity trajectory but no relief until 2027-2028.

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns Q3 2026 DRAM prices up 20-30%, NAND up 35-40%; memory rally extends into fifth quarter
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="16-13,16-14">ADATA Chairman stated DRAM contract prices expected to rise 20-30% in Q3, with NAND Flash prices up 35-40%.</cite> <cite index="17-1,17-2">TrendForce forecast aligns, projecting DRAM contract prices +13-18% Q3, NAND +10-15% QoQ.</cite> Module makers passing through supplier price increases; confirms no demand destruction at enterprise level despite consumer weakness.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: HBM contract prices could double in 2027 as DRAM shortage intensifies; HBM to consume 30% of wafer starts
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="9-1,9-5,9-10">Industry consensus points toward manufacturers sharply raising HBM quotes in 2027, with potential for prices to double; HBM will account for 30% of total DRAM wafer starts in 2027, intensifying crowding-out effect on conventional DRAM.</cite> <cite index="9-13,9-14">Downstream customers exhibit relatively low price sensitivity, more focused on supply stability; HBM's high value-add will become core driver of revenue growth and profit improvement.</cite> Bullish for both Samsung and SK Hynix margin trajectory.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $725B, up 77% YoY and nearly double mid-2025 consensus of $365B
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="27-1,27-5,27-8">Consensus estimates for 2026 capex now $725 billion, nearly double last year's estimate of $365 billion; capex rising faster than operating cash flow, driving funding needs.</cite> <cite index="20-3,20-6">Goldman expects combined $5.3 trillion capex spending for Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet from FY2025-2030; the four collectively plan to allocate $725 billion in 2026.</cite> Sustains memory demand through 2027 despite equity market volatility and ROI debate.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as capacity hits 120-130K wpm
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="30-1,30-2">TSMC CoWoS capacity projected to reach 120,000-130,000 wpm by end-2026, up from 13,000 wpm at end-2023, roughly 10x expansion driven by NVIDIA B200/GB200 and AMD MI300X/MI400 demand.</cite> <cite index="31-10">CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from around 20% currently to about 10% by end-2026.</cite> Eases one bottleneck but HBM supply remains the binding constraint for AI accelerator production through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix shares drop 7-14% in July selloff tracking U.S. chip rout; profit-taking amid AI spending concerns
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="41-10,41-11,41-13">Samsung tumbled 7-9% while SK Hynix sank 9-14.57%, wiping out billions in market value as Asia's largest chipmakers bore brunt of global tech selloff.</cite> <cite index="47-11,47-16,47-17">Decline follows U.S. session overnight; recent pullback reflects how crowded semiconductor trades have become, with semiconductors now making up roughly 20% of S&P 500.</cite> Fundamentals intact but positioning stretched; creates better entry for long-term holders.

news_pulse.headline: Server DDR5 profitability overtakes HBM for first time in Q1 2026; memory suppliers gain pricing leverage on conventional DRAM
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="8-2,8-3">Server DDR5 pricing surpassed HBM profitability since early 2026—a historic first driven by rapid ASP escalation.</cite> <cite index="9-3,9-16,9-17">With HBM's per-wafer revenue and profit margins overtaken by DDR5 64GB RDIMM, manufacturers will adjust capacity allocation based on final negotiated prices.</cite> Gives Samsung and SK Hynix optionality to maximize margin mix; reduces risk of HBM pricing collapse if AI demand falters.

brief.derivatives_signal: No listed options on 005930.KS or 000660.KS; ADR options on SSNLF (Samsung OTC) illiquid. SKHY (SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR) options launched post-July 10 debut but thin; put/call ratio 1.12 per 24/7 Wall St. suggests modest defensive tilt. Kospi 200 futures and sector ETFs (e.g., Roundhill Memory DRAM) more liquid for macro hedging. DRAM ETF off 5% July 15 per news flow; memory stock volatility spiking but no clear directional signal beyond profit-taking after YTD runs.

Nvidia, Broadcom, or hyperscaler commentary on memory allocation or pricing pass-through in earnings calls or conferences
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates for DDR5 or NAND through July 19
